summary: Two-project integration brief: Agent Loop proposes autonomous work; Tool Gate is the Rust policy library/CLI that evaluates proposed tool invocations and emits deterministic allow, deny, or review_required receipts without executing tools. Their shared safety boundary is the transition from agent intent to runtime side effects: proposals must not become execution until policy, scope, trace, idempotency, and review requirements are evaluated. Actionable integration: adapt every Agent Loop tool proposal into ToolMetadata plus InvocationEnvelope, call Tool Gate immediately before execution, execute only allow receipts, route review_required receipts to an operator, and audit all receipts. Agent Loop risk: any direct execution path that bypasses this integration defeats deterministic pre-execution enforcement. Tool Gate risk: it trusts caller-supplied metadata and is not authentication, authorization, or sandboxing, so untrusted metadata or a runtime that ignores receipts can permit unsafe effects. The declared clean-tree check passed, and no files were modified.
